dialogues.speaker: Tirda
dialogues.text: Sometimes, I'd wonder if I had been born in the wrong tribe...

dialogues.speaker: Tirda
dialogues.text: It's because I was born with a fear of heights.

dialogues.speaker: Tirda
dialogues.text: That's pretty much the worst curse you can get as a reserve member of the Qucusaur Riders.

dialogues.speaker: Tirda
dialogues.text: Knowing that, it's also no surprise that I keep failing the Rider prep exams...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sorry, can't really help you there...

dialogues.speaker: Tirda
dialogues.text: It's alright, it's not your fault.

dialogues.speaker: Tirda
dialogues.text: Yeah. But even if you weren't born with a fear of heights like me, getting through the Exams is still no walk in the park.

dialogues.speaker: Tirda
dialogues.text: Those who couldn't pass, like me, are called the "Wingless." Many of us ended up leaving the Flower-Feather Clan.

dialogues.speaker: Tirda
dialogues.text: Some Wingless are not adept at flying, but are otherwise very capable at fighting. They often find permanent work as warriors in the other tribes.

dialogues.speaker: Tirda
dialogues.text: I'm not that strong, though, so the only choice left to me was to work as a singer in this restaurant...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Heroes tend to get a chance to show their stuff.

dialogues.speaker: Tirda
dialogues.text: By that, do you mean that my singing techniques will come in useful?

dialogues.speaker: Tirda
dialogues.text: Maybe you're right. I suppose the ability to help everyone feel relaxed and happy is a gift in its own right...

dialogues.speaker: Tirda
dialogues.text: Thanks for saying that, I feel much better. Here, have some flowers. Thank you — you have no idea what a relief it was to hear your words.
